input: Submit my novel manuscript to three literary agents

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the manuscript is fully written and polished, or still in draft, determines whether the first step is editing or jumping straight to querying.
The genre and target audience of the novel dictates which agents are even relevant to approach — a middle-grade agent is useless to a literary fiction writer.
Whether the user has queried before affects how much guidance is needed on the process itself versus just the execution steps.
A target timeline (e.g., submitting within two weeks vs. three months) shapes how many agents to research at once and how to pace the work.
Knowing which submission materials are already prepared (query letter, synopsis, sample pages) identifies exactly where the work starts.
The user may have strong preferences on how to find agents — e.g., QueryTracker, Publishers Marketplace, personal recommendations — which affects the research approach.
The user's definition of a successful submission (e.g., getting a request for the full manuscript, simply hitting send on three queries) sets the bar for what 'done well' means here.

gold.taskTitle: Submit novel manuscript to three literary agents
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to query three literary agents with their novel manuscript, which involves identifying suitable agents, preparing submission materials, and sending them out.

questions.title: Is your manuscript fully written and polished for submission?
questions.description: Determine the current state of the manuscript — complete and edited, complete but unedited, or still in progress — to establish whether editing is a prerequisite step.

questions.title: What is the genre and target age group of your novel?
questions.description: Identify the specific genre (e.g., literary fiction, thriller, YA fantasy) so that agent research is targeted only to those who represent that category.

questions.title: Have you gone through the querying process before?
questions.description: Gauge the user's prior experience with literary agent submissions to calibrate how much process explanation versus direct action steps are needed.

questions.title: When do you want to send the first query out?
questions.description: Establish a target deadline or timeframe for the first submission to structure the pace of research, drafting, and revision tasks.

questions.title: Which submission materials do you already have ready?
questions.description: Find out which of the core materials — query letter, 1-page synopsis, first 10 pages, full manuscript — are already drafted so the plan starts at the right gap.

questions.title: How do you plan to find and research potential agents?
questions.description: Understand whether the user has a preferred method for sourcing agents (QueryTracker, MSWL, Publishers Marketplace, referrals, etc.) to align the research steps with tools they are comfortable using.

questions.title: What would a successful submission outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Clarify the user's personal definition of success — whether it is simply sending the queries, receiving a full manuscript request, or signing with an agent — to set the right finish line for the plan.
